group.passage:
In 1966, plant breeders at the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines produced a new variety of rice called IR8. Developed from a short rice plant from Taiwan, it gave such large harvests that people called it “miracle rice,” and it is widely credited with bringing the Green Revolution to tropical Asia.
Much of its success came from its height. IR8 was a semi-dwarf, and short plants are far less likely to fall over in the field. This allowed farmers to feed it large amounts of nitrogen fertilizer, which raised the amount of grain it produced without bringing the plants down. Before 1950, farmers in tropical Asia rarely harvested more than about 2.5 tonnes of rice per hectare. In a trial at the institute’s own farm in 1966, IR8 produced 10.3 tonnes.
Farms, however, are not test fields. At experiment stations across tropical Asia, the new rice yielded between 4 and 8 tonnes, and on ordinary farms the gains depended on things that seeds alone could not supply. Irrigation and fertilizer were essential partners of the new varieties, so the poorest areas, which relied only on rain, were the slowest to benefit. As the chart shows, average yields in tropical Asian countries did not jump overnight; they climbed step by step over several decades. The chart also includes Japan, whose farmers were already harvesting far more rice per hectare in 1961.
The overall results were still remarkable. Between 1960 and 2000, rice yields in developing countries more than doubled. Over roughly half a century, the developing world tripled its production of cereal crops while the area being farmed grew by only about 30 percent. Without improved crops, experts estimate, another 20 to 25 million hectares of land would have been needed to grow the same amount of food. Yet success came at a price. Heavy use of fertilizer, water, and farm chemicals has damaged soil and polluted water in many places, and newer varieties have struggled to raise the highest possible yield much beyond what IR8 could reach. Feeding a growing world, it seems, will take more than another miracle seed.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: How breeders in the Philippines created IR8 from a Taiwanese rice plant.
options.B: Why rice farmers in Japan have long harvested more than others.
options.C: How a new rice raised harvests, and why its gains had limits.
options.D: Why farmers who relied on rain refused to grow the new rice.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why did IR8’s short height matter?

options.A: It let farmers add more fertilizer without the plants falling over.
options.B: It let the rice grow well in places that depended on rain alone.
options.C: It meant the rice needed much less fertilizer than tall plants did.
options.D: It made the grain easier for farmers to harvest by hand.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the yields at experiment stations across tropical Asia?

options.A: To prove that IR8 did poorly outside the Philippines.
options.B: To show that IR8 did not really beat traditional rice.
options.C: To explain why farmers in Japan harvested more rice per hectare.
options.D: To show that IR8’s 1966 trial result was better than usual.

questions.stem: Which of the following is supported by both the passage and the chart?

options.A: India’s average yield more than doubled between 1970 and 1990.
options.B: In 2020, the Philippines still averaged under half of IR8’s 1966 trial yield.
options.C: Japan’s yield fell after 1970 because its farmers did not adopt IR8.
options.D: By 2000, all three tropical countries averaged at least 4 tonnes per hectare.

1.explanation_zh: 第一、二段介紹 IR8 這種「奇蹟稻米」如何靠矮小的植株和大量氮肥提高產量；第三段用 Farms, however, are not test fields 轉折，說試驗田的成績不等於一般農田，產量要靠灌溉與肥料、靠雨水的地區受惠最慢；第四段先說整體成果驚人，再用 Yet success came at a price 說明環境代價與產量瓶頸。全文講的是「新稻種如何提高收成，以及它的成果有哪些限制」。

1.strategy_zh: 主旨題留意轉折詞 however、Yet：本文先講成功、再講限制，正解要同時涵蓋兩面；只講 IR8 由來或只講圖表比較的選項都是局部。
hints: 第一、二段在講 IR8 的什麼？
第三段開頭的 however 和第四段的 Yet 之後，作者分別提醒了什麼？
哪一個選項同時包含「提高收成」和「有限制」兩面？

2.explanation_zh: 第二段說 IR8 是半矮性品種，矮的植株比較不容易倒伏，因此農民可以施用大量氮肥來提高穀粒產量，而植株不會倒下。所以矮小的重要性在於：能多施肥而不倒伏。
evidence: IR8 was a semi-dwarf, and short plants are far less likely to fall over in the field.

option_notes_zh.D: 文中沒有提到收割方式或是否方便用手收割。

2.strategy_zh: 因果題要找 This allowed… 這類句子：This 指前一句「矮的植株不容易倒伏」，allowed 後面就是結果（能施大量氮肥）。小心和常識一致、卻和原文相反的選項。

evidence: In a trial at the institute’s own farm in 1966, IR8 produced 10.3 tonnes.
Farms, however, are not test fields.
At experiment stations across tropical Asia, the new rice yielded between 4 and 8 tonnes, and on ordinary farms the gains depended on things that seeds alone could not supply.

option_notes_zh.A: 說過頭：4 到 8 公噸仍遠高於 1950 年以前熱帶亞洲大約 2.5 公噸的水準，不能說表現很差。
option_notes_zh.B: 與原文相反：試驗站的 4 到 8 公噸高於傳統稻米很少超過的 2.5 公噸，IR8 確實比傳統稻米好。
option_notes_zh.C: 細節錯置：日本的高產量是在同一段最後一句另外提到的圖表比較，和試驗站的結果無關。

A: Before 1950, farmers in tropical Asia rarely harvested more than about 2.5 tonnes of rice per hectare.
B: Before 1950, farmers in tropical Asia rarely harvested more than about 2.5 tonnes of rice per hectare.
At experiment stations across tropical Asia, the new rice yielded between 4 and 8 tonnes, and on ordinary farms the gains depended on things that seeds alone could not supply.

3.strategy_zh: 引述目的題先看它和前文的關係：前一段的 10.3 公噸是「最好的試驗結果」，however 之後的 4 到 8 公噸是「各地的一般結果」。再把數字和 2.5 公噸比較，就能排除「IR8 其實沒比較好」這類選項。

option_notes_zh.C: 日本 1970 到 1980 年的產量確實下降，但文中沒有說日本是否採用 IR8，也沒有說下降的原因。

4.strategy_zh: 「圖文都支持」的題目要兩邊對照：先從文中找出條件（IR8 試驗產量 10.3），再到圖上找數值（菲律賓 2020 年 4.09）動手計算；「加倍」用除法、「至少 4 公噸」要每一國都檢查，含因果的選項還要確認文中真的說了原因。
hints: IR8 在 1966 年試驗中的產量是多少？它的一半是多少？

translation_zh.text:
1966 年，位於菲律賓的國際稻米研究所的育種人員培育出一種名為 IR8 的新稻米品種。它是由一種來自台灣的矮稈稻米培育而成，收成多到人們稱它為「奇蹟稻米」，一般認為它把綠色革命帶進了熱帶亞洲。
它的成功很大一部分來自它的高度。IR8 是半矮性品種，而矮的植株在田裡比較不容易倒伏。這讓農民可以施用大量氮肥，提高穀粒的產量，而植株不會倒下。1950 年以前，熱帶亞洲的農民每公頃稻米的收成很少超過大約 2.5 公噸。1966 年在研究所自己農場的一次試驗中，IR8 收成了 10.3 公噸。
然而，農田不是試驗田。在熱帶亞洲各地的試驗站，這種新稻米每公頃收成 4 到 8 公噸；而在一般農田，收成的提高要靠種子本身無法提供的條件。灌溉和肥料是新品種不可少的搭檔，因此只靠雨水的最貧窮地區受惠最慢。如圖表所示，熱帶亞洲國家的平均產量並非一夕暴增，而是在數十年間一步步攀升。圖表也列出日本，日本農民在 1961 年每公頃的稻米收成就已經高出許多。
儘管如此，整體成果仍然驚人。1960 年到 2000 年間，開發中國家的稻米單位產量增加了一倍以上。在大約半個世紀裡，開發中世界的穀物產量增為三倍，耕地面積卻只增加約 30%。專家估計，如果沒有改良作物，要種出同樣多的糧食，還得多用 2,000 萬到 2,500 萬公頃的土地。然而成功是有代價的。大量使用肥料、水和農藥，已經在許多地方破壞土壤、汙染水源；而較新的品種也很難把最高可能產量提高到比 IR8 高出很多。看來，要養活成長中的世界，需要的不只是另一顆奇蹟種子。
【圖】四個亞洲國家的稻米單位面積產量（1961–2020，公噸／公頃）：印度、印尼、菲律賓、日本。

open_tasks.prompt: The passage ends by saying that feeding a growing world will take more than another miracle seed. Besides better seeds, what else do farmers need? Answer in 1–2 English sentences and use one idea from the passage.
reference_answers: Farmers also need a steady supply of water, because the passage shows that areas that relied only on rain were the slowest to benefit.
Farmers need to use fertilizer and chemicals more carefully, since heavy use has damaged soil and polluted water in many places.
